title: Towards Surrogate Based Dequantization of Quantum Reinforcement Learning
authors: Pablo Rodriguez-Grasa, Sofiene Jerbi, Mikel Sanz, Ryan Sweke
abstract: In recent years, the utility of parameterized quantum circuits as function approximators has been widely studied. In the context of reinforcement learning, this approach has led to variational quantum algorithms such as quantum Q-learning. While these methods show promising empirical results, and can provide provable advantages for artificial problems, it remains unclear whether they can provide a provable quantum advantage over classical approaches for problems of practical relevance. A natural way to investigate this question is through the lens of dequantization: The construction of efficient classical algorithms capable of matching the performance of quantum variational methods. Building on recent kernel-based dequantization results for supervised learning, we take steps towards extending this surrogate-based dequantization program to reinforcement learning. Specifically, we study the simplified setting of reinforcement learning with a uniform generative model in which uniformly random state-action samples are available, which models the regime of sampling from a large experience replay buffer after sufficient exploration. Within this setting, we provide finite sample guarantees for classical kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration, with classical kernels designed to match the inductive bias of particular parameterized quantum circuits. Using these results, we then provide a set of sufficient conditions, on the data-encoding strategy of a parameterized quantum circuit, the corresponding classical kernel, and the problem structure, under which kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration provides a meaningful dequantization of quantum Q-learning, in this simplified setting. Apart from providing rigorous dequantization guarantees when these conditions are met, these results also motivate the use of kernelized fitted Q-iteration as a dequantization heuristic when these sufficient conditions cannot be verified.
summary: This paper tackles the theoretical question of whether Quantum Q-learning offers a true quantum advantage by developing a surrogate-based dequantization program. By restricting the problem to a simplified sampling regime, the authors prove that classical kernel methods can effectively mimic the quantum performance under specific structural conditions. This work provides rigorous theoretical bounds on the potential quantum advantage in reinforcement learning.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether quantum reinforcement learning algorithms, specifically Quantum Q-learning, can be theoretically matched in performance by efficient classical algorithms (dequantization).
main_result: Under a simplified setting (uniform generative model), the authors provide finite sample guarantees showing that classical kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration can provide a meaningful dequantization of Quantum Q-learning, suggesting no exponential quantum advantage in this regime.
method: The core method is surrogate-based dequantization, extending kernel-based techniques from supervised learning to the reinforcement learning setting using classical kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI).
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Reinforcement Learning (RL), where Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs) act as function approximators for the Q-function. The analysis is simplified by assuming access to uniformly random state-action samples.
key_observables: The primary observable is the performance gap between the quantum and classical approaches, quantified by relative dequantization bounds ($	ext{Loss}[h_c] \le 	ext{Loss}[h_q] + \epsilon$).
important_parameters: The analysis is restricted to the simplified setting of a uniform generative model, and the results depend on sufficient conditions related to the kernel and PQC structure.
main_assumptions: The rigorous guarantees are conditional on identifying sufficient structural conditions relating the data-encoding strategy, the classical kernel, and the problem structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining dequantization notions, reviewing the RL/Q-learning context, introducing PQCs, simplifying the setting to uniform sampling, developing the classical kernelized FQI algorithm, and finally proving finite sample guarantees and sufficient conditions for dequantization.
why_interesting: While focused on RL, the theoretical framework of dequantization—determining when quantum computational advantages are merely artifacts of model expressivity rather than fundamental physical speedups—is highly relevant to understanding the limits of quantum algorithms in general.
